criterion: A hop to a profile that cannot start is refused in the same session, and the running session keeps going.
evidence: cli/hop.go hopModelRefusal refuses before the relay signal is written or the session is TERMed, and the gate round closed its three gaps: a warm cache for a model the current listing no longer serves no longer counts as pickable (adapter.AutoPickable mirrors classify: only listing-served models decide), a 404 listing with no saved or recoverable model is refused before anything closes, and a model the conversation itself recovers (a transcript turn with a model but no effort) no longer blocks a hop the relay pass would land. tests/ccmorph_test.zsh: test_a_hop_to_a_profile_that_cannot_pick_a_model_is_refused_in_session_issue_379 (refusal half, stale-cache half, declared-listing guard half), test_a_hop_to_an_endpoint_with_no_model_list_is_refused_in_session_issue_379, test_a_hop_that_recovers_a_model_from_the_conversation_is_not_refused_issue_379 — all three scenarios watched red on the phase-1 core first. CCMORPH_TEST_FILTER=hop: 21 PASS, 0 failures (switch: 8, relay: 9).

criterion: When a hop to a profile with no saved model cannot choose one, the message names the command that lists the models (`ccmorph models strict`) next to the command that saves one.
evidence: The pick refusal reads "no model is set and none can be picked from its model list; list them: ccmorph models strict, then save one: ccmorph set strict model <model-id>" — asserted (including on the stale-cache rerun) by the zsh test. The 404 refusal names only the save command ("the endpoint offers no model list (HTTP 404) and no model is set, so a hop here needs a saved model; save one: ccmorph set strict model <model-id>") and the zsh test asserts the listing command is NOT named there: an endpoint with no model list cannot answer it (INTENT: a refusal gives a truthful reason). The adapter's own refusals carry the same pairs (serve refusal, 404 EXIT), pinned in phase 1.

criterion: The message uses plain words and does not mention a model protocol or a compatibility check.
evidence: The zsh test asserts the pick refusal contains neither 'protocol' nor 'compatibility check'; the new 404 message uses the same plain words as the adapter's own EXIT line. Phase-1 pins stand: TestAModelMustBeNamed*, TestAWarmCacheIsNotAModelChoice, TestARefusedListing (go test ./adapter/ -run 'TestAModelMustBeNamed|TestAWarmCacheIsNotAModelChoice|TestARefusedListing|TestAutoPickable|TestTranslatorVerdict': PASS).

criterion: `ccmorph doctor strict` says that a hop will need a saved model, or the hop works without one.
evidence: util/doctor.go adapterLine: the hop warning now fires whenever no model is set and the listing leaves the adapter nothing to pick — including the stale-cache shape the gate flagged (a cached usable model the listing no longer serves decides nothing), which previously printed 'needs no translator' and skipped the warning; an open session on the profile still answers first. The verdict row prints only where the launch could act on it (Pickable, computed by the same read-only cache+listing the launch reads). Pinned by TestAdapterLine's stale/pickable/open-session cases (go test ./util/ -run TestAdapterLine: PASS) and tests/doctor_test.py test_doctor_adapter_line_states_the_need_issue_272, now five cases: the two cache cases got listings that serve the cached model (the GH-272 verdict pin, unchanged), plus two stale cases that expect the INFO hop row (CCMORPH_LIB_DIR=$PWD/lib pytest tests/doctor_test.py -q: 96 passed; the only 3 failures are the pre-existing sandbox pty/network ones GH-363's acceptance noted). The other branch holds: the zsh guard half hops with no saved model when the listing declares a chat endpoint and the switch proceeds.
